title: Who a step-up suits less
objectives: Name the client types a percentage step-up suits less.
Offer the alternative that fits each.
body_md:
A step-up is not for everyone, and saying so early builds trust.

## Who it suits less

- Retirees on a fixed income: the instalment would rise while income does not.
- Clients with very irregular earnings: a fixed-amount step-up or occasional lump sums fit better.
- Goals only 1–3 years away: a step-up adds little, and the money may need to move to debt.

## The alternatives

- Fixed-amount step-up at a small, predictable rate.
- A second, smaller SIP started each year instead of an automatic step-up.
- Lump sums or an STP when a bonus or inheritance arrives.

## The judgement to make

The question is never "can the client afford a bigger SIP today?" It is "can the client afford every future instalment without cancelling?" A smaller, automatic step-up beats an ambitious one that gets stopped.
example: A consultant with uneven quarterly income sets a fixed +₹500 step-up rather than 10%, and tops up with a lump sum in her best month.
say: A smaller step-up you'll keep beats a bigger one you'll cancel.
With irregular income, a fixed amount or an extra SIP each year may fit better.
never: Everyone should step up 10% a year.
A retiree should step up to beat inflation.

talk_track.title: Who a step-up suits less
talk_track.text: A step-up suits clients whose income is likely to grow. It suits retirees on fixed income less, and clients with very irregular earnings, where a fixed-amount step-up or occasional lump sums may fit better. Goals only one to three years away gain little from a step-up.

check.q: Which client does a percentage step-up suit least?
o: A retiree on a fixed pension
A business owner whose income grows
check.why: A fixed pension does not grow, so the instalment would rise while income does not.

check.q: What is a good alternative for a client with irregular income?
o: A fixed-amount step-up, a second SIP each year, or lump sums
check.why: Predictable, small increases fit irregular income better than a percentage rule.

check.q: What is the real question before recommending a step-up?
o: Can the client afford a bigger SIP today?
Can the client afford every future instalment without cancelling?
What did the fund return last year?
How many SIPs does the client hold?
check.why: Sustainability is the test, not today's affordability.
